paper.title: A semi-supervised learning approach to predict synthetic genetic interactions by combining functional and topological properties of functional gene network
paper.citation: You ZH, Yin Z, Han K, Huang DS, Zhou X. A semi-supervised learning approach to predict synthetic genetic interactions by combining functional and topological properties of functional gene network. BMC Bioinformatics 11:343 (2010)

inputs.name: Additional file 1 (1471-2105-11-343-S1.DOC, read, not used by the pipeline)

items.label: Fig. 1, workflow schematic

cause.summary: A diagram of the workflow; nothing is computed.

items.label: Abstract and Results: sensitivity 92% at specificity 91% (TPR 0.92 at FPR 0.09)

assumptions.what: Protein interactions: BioGRID two-hybrid and Affinity Capture-Western interactions of S. cerevisiae as SGD imported them on 2009-12-19 (13,007 interactions, 3,915 proteins; the paper has 12,990 and 4,478). Chosen as the interpretable filter closest to the paper's interaction count in a search over experiment-type subsets; it matches that one count only. The release's genetic interactions cover {{counts.genetic_genes}} genes, close to the paper's 4,478.
assumptions.sensitivity: Every physical interaction instead: SSL {{hypotheses.ppi_all.ssl.auc}}, SVM {{hypotheses.ppi_all.svm.auc}} against {{hypotheses.baseline.ssl.auc}} and {{hypotheses.baseline.svm.auc}} (Fig. 3 setting, repeat 0).

assumptions.what: Eq. 2's W used as the tie strength (the paper calls it a confidence score) and inverted for shortest paths; the published Fig. 6 and Fig. S18 axes (weighted degrees in the hundreds, closeness above 1) fit this reading.
assumptions.sensitivity: 1 / W instead: SSL {{hypotheses.inverse_weights.ssl.auc}}, SVM {{hypotheses.inverse_weights.svm.auc}} (Fig. 3 setting, repeat 0; baseline SSL {{hypotheses.baseline.ssl.auc}}, SVM {{hypotheses.baseline.svm.auc}}).

assumptions.what: Features: sign(x) log(1 + |x|), then z-scored (the paper does not say how features were scaled).
assumptions.sensitivity: Without the log: SSL {{hypotheses.no_log.ssl.auc}}, SVM {{hypotheses.no_log.svm.auc}} (Fig. 3 setting, repeat 0; baseline SSL {{hypotheses.baseline.ssl.auc}}, SVM {{hypotheses.baseline.svm.auc}}).

assumptions.what: SSL: alpha = 0.99 (Zhou et al.'s value); sigma chosen among 0.05, 0.1, 0.2, 0.5 and 1 times the median distance by hiding a third of the training labels.
assumptions.sensitivity: sigma = the median distance: SSL {{hypotheses.median_sigma.ssl.auc}}; alpha = 0.5: {{hypotheses.alpha_0.5.ssl.auc}} (Fig. 3 setting, repeat 0; baseline SSL {{hypotheses.baseline.ssl.auc}}, SVM {{hypotheses.baseline.svm.auc}}).

assumptions.what: SVM: scikit-learn 1.6.1 SVC (LIBSVM), RBF kernel, C in 2^-1..2^9 and gamma in 2^-9..2^1 (steps of 4x), 3-fold grid search on the training folds by area under the ROC curve.

The 18 features: the average and the absolute difference of 8 node properties (weighted degree, Barrat clustering, betweenness, closeness, eigenvector centrality; binary stress, information and current-flow betweenness), the weighted shortest path, and the number of mutual neighbours.

Non-SGI pairs: Tong 2004 query genes x the deletion array (Verified and Uncharacterized ORFs without an inviable systematic deletion, 4,747 genes) with no reported Tong 2004 interaction, both genes in the network.
assumptions.sensitivity: Random gene pairs instead: SSL {{hypotheses.random_negatives.ssl.auc}}, SVM {{hypotheses.random_negatives.svm.auc}} (Fig. 3 setting, repeat 0; baseline SSL {{hypotheses.baseline.ssl.auc}}, SVM {{hypotheses.baseline.svm.auc}}).

assumptions.what: Five repeats with seeds 0-4; test scores ranked within each fold and pooled; repeats averaged at 26 score quantiles (threshold averaging), which also place the drawn markers.

Expression: SGD's processed copies of Cho 1998 (17 conditions), Chu 1998 sporulation (7), Spellman 1998 alpha factor (16) and elutriation (14): 54 conditions, not 64. Eisen 1998's 6 heat-shock points were not reachable.

cause.summary: Not reproduced with the network the Methods describe (protein interactions and complexes): areas under the ROC curve {{roc.curves.unlabelled20/ssl/weighted.auc_mean:.3f}} to {{roc.curves.unlabelled80/ssl/weighted.auc_mean:.3f}} for SSL and {{roc.curves.unlabelled20/svm/weighted.auc_mean:.3f}} to {{roc.curves.unlabelled80/svm/weighted.auc_mean:.3f}} for SVM; the published curves enclose {{comparison.fig2.published_auc_read.blue}}, {{comparison.fig3.published_auc_read.blue}} and {{comparison.fig4.published_auc_read.blue}} (SSL) and {{comparison.fig2.published_auc_read.red}}, {{comparison.fig3.published_auc_read.red}} and {{comparison.fig4.published_auc_read.red}} (SVM), read from Figs 2-4. The published level comes back once BioGRID's genetic interactions are in the network (Fig. 3 setting: SSL {{hypotheses.genetic_other.ssl.auc}}, SVM {{hypotheses.genetic_other.svm.auc}} without Tong 2004's own rows, {{hypotheses.genetic_all.ssl.auc}} and {{hypotheses.genetic_all.svm.auc}} with them); these edges carry the SGI labels into the features. Open: the authors' exact network, and the order of the two classifiers (SVM stays ahead of SSL in every variant we ran).

hypotheses.hypothesis: Our classifier settings are off: the SSL length scale or alpha.
hypotheses.test: Fig. 3 setting, repeat 0: SSL with sigma = the median distance (no selection), and with alpha = 0.5 instead of 0.99. SSL area under the ROC curve {{hypotheses.median_sigma.ssl.auc}} and {{hypotheses.alpha_0.5.ssl.auc}} against {{hypotheses.baseline.ssl.auc}}; the published curves enclose {{comparison.fig2.published_auc_read.blue}}, {{comparison.fig3.published_auc_read.blue}} and {{comparison.fig4.published_auc_read.blue}} (SSL) and {{comparison.fig2.published_auc_read.red}}, {{comparison.fig3.published_auc_read.red}} and {{comparison.fig4.published_auc_read.red}} (SVM) at 20, 50 and 80% unlabelled, read from Figs 2-4.

hypotheses.hypothesis: Our protein-interaction filter is wrong (the paper gives only 'BioGrid').
hypotheses.test: Every physical interaction except Gavin's and Ho's (44,346 edges) in place of two-hybrid plus Affinity Capture-Western. SSL {{hypotheses.ppi_all.ssl.auc}}, SVM {{hypotheses.ppi_all.svm.auc}} (ours {{hypotheses.baseline.ssl.auc}}, {{hypotheses.baseline.svm.auc}}).

hypotheses.hypothesis: Eq. 2's W is a distance, so the tie strength is 1 / W.
hypotheses.test: Weighted network rebuilt with 1 / W. SSL {{hypotheses.inverse_weights.ssl.auc}}, SVM {{hypotheses.inverse_weights.svm.auc}}.

hypotheses.hypothesis: Our feature scaling hides the signal.
hypotheses.test: Features z-scored without the log transform. SSL {{hypotheses.no_log.ssl.auc}}, SVM {{hypotheses.no_log.svm.auc}}.

hypotheses.hypothesis: The non-SGI pairs were random gene pairs, not tested pairs.
hypotheses.test: 1,500 random pairs of network genes (no reported SGI) as negatives. SSL {{hypotheses.random_negatives.ssl.auc}}, SVM {{hypotheses.random_negatives.svm.auc}} (Fig. 3 setting, repeat 0; baseline SSL {{hypotheses.baseline.ssl.auc}}, SVM {{hypotheses.baseline.svm.auc}}): higher, but far from the published curves.

hypotheses.hypothesis: Our network measures are computed wrongly.
hypotheses.test: Stress, current-flow betweenness and information centrality checked against networkx and a brute-force path count on random graphs (package tests).

hypotheses.hypothesis: The paper's pair-level cross-validation lets a gene's identity carry from training to test pairs: each Tong query gene sits in many pairs.
hypotheses.test: SVM and SSL on one-hot gene identity alone, no network: SSL {{hypotheses.gene_identity.ssl.auc}}, SVM {{hypotheses.gene_identity.svm.auc}} (Fig. 3 setting, repeat 0; baseline SSL {{hypotheses.baseline.ssl.auc}}, SVM {{hypotheses.baseline.svm.auc}}). Every test pair shares a gene with the training pairs ({{hypotheses.gene_identity.test_pairs_with_one_gene_in_training}} of them), {{hypotheses.gene_identity.test_pairs_with_both_genes_in_training}} share both. A problem with the paper's evaluation: its AUCs measure, in part, which genes are SGI hubs.

hypotheses.hypothesis: The authors' 'BioGrid' network included genetic interactions. Many Tong SGI pairs are reported again by other papers ({{counts.sgi_pairs_reported_by_other_papers}} of {{counts.sgi_pairs}}), so the labels become edges of the network.
hypotheses.test: Our network plus the genetic interactions of papers other than Tong 2004 ({{hypotheses.genetic_other.edges}} edges; {{hypotheses.genetic_other.sample_sgi_pairs_that_are_edges}} of the 1,500 sampled SGI pairs and {{hypotheses.genetic_other.sample_nonsgi_pairs_that_are_edges}} non-SGI pairs become edges): SSL {{hypotheses.genetic_other.ssl.auc}}, SVM {{hypotheses.genetic_other.svm.auc}} (Fig. 3 setting, repeat 0; baseline SSL {{hypotheses.baseline.ssl.auc}}, SVM {{hypotheses.baseline.svm.auc}}); the published Fig. 3 curves enclose {{comparison.fig3.published_auc_read.blue}} (SSL) and {{comparison.fig3.published_auc_read.red}} (SVM). With every genetic interaction, Tong 2004 included: SSL {{hypotheses.genetic_all.ssl.auc}}, SVM {{hypotheses.genetic_all.svm.auc}}. Suggested by a reviewer (hyunhwan-bcm) on the pull request.

hypotheses.hypothesis: Genetic interactions help beyond the leaked labels (genes with many genetic partners are SGI hubs).
hypotheses.test: The same network with every Tong SGI pair removed from the added edges: SSL {{hypotheses.genetic_other_no_tong_pairs.ssl.auc}}, SVM {{hypotheses.genetic_other_no_tong_pairs.svm.auc}}.

page.claims_line: Main claim, SSL beats SVM and reaches sensitivity 0.92 at 1 minus specificity 0.09: {{verdict.text.ssl_above_svm}}. With the network the Methods describe (protein interactions and complexes) SVM leads at every training size and the best SSL sensitivity at 0.09 is {{claims.text.operating_point.fields.0.observed}}. The published accuracy comes back once BioGRID's genetic interactions are in the network, and these carry the SGI labels into it (Fig. 3 setting: SSL {{hypotheses.genetic_other.ssl.auc}}, SVM {{hypotheses.genetic_other.svm.auc}}); SVM still leads. The paper's pair-level cross-validation also lets gene identity alone reach {{hypotheses.gene_identity.svm.auc}}. Weighted beats binary: {{verdict.text.weighted_above_binary}}, by a small margin. Two Discussion claims fail in the paper's own Table 1.
came_back: SGD's copy of BioGRID of 2009-12-19: {{counts.complex_interactions}} complex edges against about 49,000 and {{counts.array_genes}} deletion-array genes against about 4,700 agree; {{counts.sgi_pairs}} Tong SGI pairs (about 4,000), {{counts.tong_queries}} query genes (132) and {{counts.ppi_proteins}} PPI proteins (4,478) do not.
Divisive correlation clustering, eq. 2 weights, the 10 properties and 18 features, label spreading and an RBF SVM, as the package fgnssl.

SGI pairs have the higher median average degree and closeness, as the Discussion says; the closeness difference is not significant on our run.
Why the paper's numbers are so high

With BioGRID's genetic interactions in the network the AUC reaches the published level; {{counts.sgi_pairs_reported_by_other_papers}} of the {{counts.sgi_pairs}} Tong SGI pairs are themselves genetic-interaction edges reported by other papers. Gene identity alone reaches {{hypotheses.gene_identity.svm.auc}} under the paper's pair-level cross-validation.
